Profile the structure of an object

Source: R/contract_profile.R
profileObject.Rd

Describe the structure of any R object (S4, lists, environments, matrices, tables) as a flat node table, without loading the package that defines it. Profiles are used to choose a mapping, to compute structural fingerprints and to detect drift between object versions.

Usage

profileObject(
  x,
  max_depth = 8L,
  max_children = 50L,
  sample_n = 10000L,
  n_cells = NULL,
  n_feat = NULL
)

Arguments

x

object to profile

max_depth

maximum depth walked

max_children

maximum number of named children walked per node; unnamed lists are represented by their first element only

sample_n

maximum number of values inspected per matrix or vector for role hints

n_cells, n_feat

optional known numbers of cells and features. When NULL they are inferred from the largest count-like matrix.

Value

a giottoProfile: a list with source, profiled_at, profiler_version, n_cells, n_feat, size_from, notes and nodes (a data.frame with columns path, kind, class, dtype, shape, n_children, truncated, role_hints, sample, value; value holds scalar vectors and is not part of the fingerprint)

Examples

p <- profileObject(list(counts = matrix(1:6, 2), meta = data.frame(a = 1:3)))
p
